tagline.text: The largest island of the Concepcion archipelago, crowned by the cone of Mt. Manaphag

location.label: Location
location.text: Off the coast of Concepcion, Iloilo Province

budget.label: Budget
budget.text: About ₱2,000–3,500 (per person, 2 days 1 night from Iloilo)

children.text: Pan de Azucar is an island of about 18.4 square kilometers off Concepcion in Iloilo Province, and the cone of Mt. Manaphag, about 574 m high, is its landmark. It suits a simple island trip: stay one night in a beach cottage and visit the sandbars of nearby Agho and Bulubadiangan.
Pan de Azucar Island lies in the Visayan Sea northeast of Panay, about
13km
northeast of Concepcion town proper and about
4km

east of mainland Panay. Its area is about 18.4 square kilometers, making it the largest of the 16 outlying islands of Concepcion. The name is Spanish for sugarloaf and comes from the shape of the conical mountain in the middle of the island.

The island has three barangays, Tambaliza, Talotu-an and Macatunao, and 7,502 residents in the 2015 census. It is also called Tampisaw Island or Tambaliza Island. The highest point is Mt. Manaphag (Mt. Pan de Azucar); sources give 573 to 574 m (a mountaineering site says 606 m), so we use about

. It is described as an inactive volcanic cone. The waters around the island are known as the Pan de Azucar Seascape; local officials treat it as a sanctuary, but the national government is said not to have declared it an official protected area.

Beaches ring the island. In Bagotao, Macatunao, Lumpatan beach has sand ranging from golden yellow to white, and Tambaliza beach has the cluster of cottage resorts. The Lumpatan rock formation is a stretch of wave-shaped rock, and the village has built a walking trail along the cliff. Hampangan Rock, a sunset viewpoint, can be reached in about
20 minutes

with a guide. As for history, one story says that in the 1600s Captain Juan Salagao, then mayor of Sugbu, defeated Spanish forces who had come from Mindanao to burn Arevalo and Octong near here. In November 2013 Typhoon Haiyan passed directly over the island, damaging houses, food stores and fishing boats, and the military delivered relief goods. Fishing is the main livelihood, followed by small-scale farming of rice, corn, vegetables, bamboo and coconuts. In 2012 a mining company was reported to have begun exploratory drilling for gold, silver, copper and zinc, and concerns were raised that the natural scenery could be harmed.

This is not a luxury island trip. The islands of Concepcion have no hotels, only basic cottages; electricity goes off at night in some places and there are no ATMs. In exchange you get quiet beaches with no shops or clubs, clear water and village life as it is. Every year in the fourth week of April, the Tampisaw Festival is held on several of Concepcion's islands and brings more visitors.

blocks.title: Views and hike on Mt. Manaphag

children.text: This is the island's landmark cone, about

high. From the top you can reportedly see the whole Concepcion archipelago. However, it is described as very steep with an unclear trail, and accidents have been mentioned, so do not climb without a guide.
A sunset viewpoint with a view of the islands and Mt. Manaphag, reached on foot in about
20 minutes
with a guide. In a 2018 review the guide cost ₱300 (split between two). It is an alternative for travelers who find Mt. Manaphag too much.
A stretch of coast where wave-shaped layers of rock stack up. On days with strong waves it is hard to land a boat; the village has built a walking trail along the cliff.
This is the beach with the most places to stay on the island. At low tide you can walk part of the beach, and reviewers say the halo-halo that children come to sell is a treat.
A small island you can visit while island hopping, with white sand and blue-green water, and a view of Mt. Manaphag and Sombrero Island together. You can rent a tent and camp overnight.
A sandbar formed by currents meeting from both sides is fully exposed at low tide. From here you can see Igbon Island and Mt. Manaphag, and you can rest in a cottage by day or a tent at night.
A 2018 review describes a route that covers Lumpatan, Agho and Bulubadiangan and returns to town. You rent a boat and do it in one day.

items.title: Basic 2 days 1 night course
items.subtitle: Go in on the scheduled boat and finish with island hopping

children.text: Take a bus bound for Concepcion from the Tagbak terminal in Jaro, Iloilo City. A 2018 review says it takes about 2.5 to 3 hours, and the scheduled boat from the town fish port to the island is said to leave once a day around
The boat takes about
30–45 minutes
to reach Tambaliza beach. Drop your bags at your cottage, have lunch and walk around the beach and village.
Climb Hampangan Rock with a guide and watch the sunset. You can also take in the Lumpatan coastal trail.
Have dinner at your cottage. Power goes off around 10 p.m. in some places, so bring a flashlight.
Rent a boat to visit Lumpatan, Agho and Bulubadiangan, then return to Concepcion town. Reviewers say the last bus is around 3 to 4 p.m., so do not dawdle.
Boats run only about once a day, and if you miss one you stay another day. Ask the Concepcion tourism office about your schedule in advance.

items.title: Course with a climb
items.subtitle: If you are aiming for Mt. Manaphag

children.text: Arrive in Concepcion and stay one night in town, or take an afternoon boat to the island and sleep at Tambaliza.
Arrange a local guide through the tourism office and set out at dawn. In a 2009 account it took about 3 to 4 hours to the summit.
Many sections are steep, so you need long clothes, gloves and sturdy shoes. After coming down, rest on the beach.
Leave the island in time for the scheduled boat.
The climbing information is mostly from a 2009 account, so trail conditions today may differ. Be sure to ask the local office for the latest situation.
Fly from Manila to Iloilo International Airport (ILO). Check flight information in the airline's app.
It is about
97km
from Iloilo City to Concepcion, and about
101km
if you come from Roxas City.

Take a Ceres bus to Concepcion from the Tagbak bus terminal in Iloilo City (Jaro). A 2018 review says it takes about 2.5 to 3 hours and costs about ₱125, and a 2016 guide says ₱110, so confirm the fare locally.
UV Express vans also run and, per 2022 information, take about
2.5 to 3.5 hours
. Get off at the Concepcion public market or town proper.
Buses run from 6 a.m. to about 3 p.m., and reviewers say the last bus back is around 3 to 4 p.m.
The scheduled boat from Concepcion fish port to Pan de Azucar is said to run once a day, leaving around
, with a return from the island at dawn. The fare is about ₱35. A 2025 itinerary lists a different timetable (departures at 8 a.m. and 4 p.m., returns at 6 a.m. and 1 p.m.), so confirm locally.

Chartering a boat cost about ₱1,500 round trip for 5–8 people per 2022 information, ₱1,500–2,500 for 4–6 people per 2025 information, and ₱1,500–2,000 (4–5 people) for a resort boat per a 2018 review. The crossing takes about
15–45 minutes
depending on the island.
Each island charges an entrance fee of around ₱25 plus an environmental fee.
You can walk around Tambaliza beach and the village.
Walk to Hampangan Rock or Mt. Manaphag with a guide.
The dry season from November to May is best, with a calm sea and clear skies. Boats are steadier then and the view from Mt. Manaphag is good. Sources also say weekdays are quieter than weekends.

From June to October there is more rain and the waves are higher, so boats can be rough or stop running. Concepcion receives about 1,258 mm of rain a year, with June to October said to be the wettest months and February to April the driest.

children.text: Prices are approximate as of
and may vary with local conditions.

Accommodation on Pan de Azucar is cottages, not hotels. In a 2018 review, a semi-enclosed cottage at Junbee Island Resort on Tambaliza beach cost ₱500, with a shared toilet and shower and electricity from 6 a.m. to 10 p.m. On nearby Bulubadiangan Island, 2022 information lists an open cottage at ₱400 (day use) to ₱800 (overnight), a semi-enclosed cottage at ₱1,000 and tent rental at ₱500. You can also rent a tent on Agho Island.

You can order meals as a group through your accommodation or bring ingredients and cook your own. In a 2018 review lunch was about ₱400, dinner about ₱400 and breakfast about ₱300. There is no ATM on the island and electricity and phone signal are weak, so bring cash and a power bank. Reviewers say the halo-halo children sell on the beach is a good snack in the midday heat.

In Concepcion town there are places to stay such as Hotel Junbee, and you can shop at the town market and around the fish port before heading out. If you miss the morning boat, staying overnight in town and leaving the next day is the comfortable choice. Meals on the island center on fresh fish and seafood, and it is best to ask the cottage owner in advance. There is almost nowhere to buy food, so stock up on snacks and water in town.
The scheduled boat runs only once a day, so check the timetable at Concepcion fish port.
Bring plenty of cash in small bills. There is no ATM on the island.
Climb Mt. Manaphag with a local guide, and ask the Concepcion tourism office about the latest situation first.
Boats cost less per person when split, so gather a group.
Plan your trip on weekdays for quieter beaches.
Bring a power bank, flashlight, water shoes and sunscreen.
The sandbars look different with the tide, so time your visit for low tide.
Mt. Manaphag is described as very steep with an unclear trail, and a past fatal fall is mentioned. Do not climb without a guide.
Prices and timetables in this guide mix 2009–2022 sources and may differ from today.
On rainy days and when waves are high the boat may not run, so leave slack in your schedule.
Electricity and phone signal on the island are limited.
Some reports note that household wastewater in some villages flows away untreated, so do not leave trash or waste behind.
There are reports of exploratory mining drilling around the island, so check the development situation locally.
A group of islands northeast of Iloilo that you reach by boat, famous for scallops and lagoons.
The hub city with the airport and bus terminal, where buses to Concepcion depart.
The main city of Capiz, about
101km
from Concepcion.
An island across the sea south of Iloilo, with mangoes and beaches.
